newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar backs down to tame close.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar backs down to tame close.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar finished a quiet session steady but off its peak after stronger-than-expected retail sales data for April.
Dealers said trade was lethargic apart from some good volume going through on the New Zealand-Australian dollar cross.
Seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 7.9 percent in April, against the top end of expectations of 5.0 percent.
That saw the Kiwi blip up to a high of around US$0.6898 but there was no shortage of people looking for rallies to sell into, which saw the currency easing to $0.6885/90 by the close.
On its Trade-Weighted Index, the currency ended at 67.71 from its 67.70 start.
